Subject: Budget range validation - Redwood + FinHub

Hi Alex / Dana,

Thanks again for the call today - great conversation and appreciate the clear signals on workload and priorities. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can size a realistic proposal: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: customer support & in-product assistant (mix of chat + reranking).
- Initial expected volume: rough ballpark 1-5M input+output tokens / month, with a mode around 2-3M as you ramp.
- 6-month plan: potential to scale to ~10-20M tokens/mo depending on pilot results.
- Latency SLO: <500ms p95 for chat; higher throughput for background reranking OK.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; data retention policies per FinHub security team.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the monthly spend band you're budgeting for this initiative (e.g. <$5k/mo, $5k-$25k/mo, $25k-$100k/mo, >$100k/mo)? That helps us recommend hosted vs Dedicated and whether a commit makes sense.
2) Procurement threshold: at what monthly or one-off spend do you need a formal PO/contract and finance approval?
3) Any target unit economics you have in mind (target $ per 1M tokens) so we can try to align pricing?

Attached a quick rough pricing one-pager to give a sense of order-of-magnitude pricing across hosted, committed, and dedicated options. I copied Rishi (pricing/BD) - he can chime in on the unit economics and commit discounts.

If it's helpful we can do a short procurement call next week to walk through contract flow and timelines.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finhub.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Redwood + FinHub

Marissa - thanks for the recap and the one-pager. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume detail: Pilot: expect 2-3M combined tokens/mo. If pilot looks good, we plan to scale to ~15M tokens/mo by month 6 (primarily chat + occasional batch rerank jobs).
- Procurement thresholds: any vendor spend above $25k/month requires VP-level approval and a PO; above $100k/mo triggers procurement/finance deep review.
- Target unit economics: for hosted APIs we'd be aiming for ~$150-$300 per 1M tokens initially (we know this is model-dependent). If committed pricing is reasonable we could consider a 6-12 month commit.

I've attached an estimate workbook with our token assumptions and expected timeline. Can Rishi propose a few pricing options (pay-as-you-go, 6-month commit, 12-month commit) and call out where Dedicated/reserved capacity becomes the better economic choice?

Also: our procurement/legal will need typical vendor info (SOC 2 report, master services agreement, liability cap, PO process). Dana is looped for procurement details.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex - great, thanks for the details and the workbook. Rishi + Dylan adding a few concrete pricing bands below so you can see how the math works against your volume ramp: 

Quick unit economics (order-of-magnitude)
- Pay-as-you-go (hosted API): $120 / 1M tokens (baseline) - good for pilots and no upfront commit.
- 6-month committed consumption (monthly billing; 20% discount): ~$96 / 1M tokens.
- 12-month committed consumption (monthly billing; 30% discount): ~$84 / 1M tokens.
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity: effective unit cost can drop below $60 / 1M tokens at higher sustained volumes (typical threshold: sustained spend >= $25k/mo or ~300-400M tokens/month depending on model mix).

Notes:
- Above numbers are model-agnostic starting points; we can provide model-specific profiles (e.g., smaller context models vs larger) which will adjust unit costs.
- For your ramp (2-3M -> 15M tokens), a 6-12 month commit would likely yield the best lift in predictability and give you predictable unit economics while keeping hosted convenience.
- Procurement threshold guidance: based on your note, if your approval trigger is $25k/mo, we can structure an initial 3-month pilot on PAYG and then move to a 6-month commit if usage crosses the threshold.

Next steps
1) I'll prepare a formal quote with three options (PAYG, 6mo commit, 12mo commit) and include the PO/vendor details and SOC 2 links for procurement.
2) Dana - can you confirm PO process (who signs, payment terms Net30/Net45) and any additional procurement docs needed?
3) If helpful, I'm happy to book a 30-min procurement + finance sync early next week to accelerate approval.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Dana Li <dana.li@finhub.com>

Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Redwood + FinHub

Marissa / Alex - procurement here. A few items to confirm so we can route to Finance: 

- PO thresholds: FinHub requires a formal PO for any recurring spend >= $25,000/month. One-off contract values >= $50,000 also require procurement review.
- Payment terms: Net30 is preferred; Net45 can be considered for annual agreements.
- Required docs: SOC 2 Type II report, certificate of insurance, vendor W9 (US), and a standard MSA with liability cap language. Please provide a point of contact in legal for quick turnaround.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly invoices tied to actual usage are preferred for PAYG; for committed deals we typically accept monthly billing against committed amount.

If you can send a formal quote with the three options Marissa mentioned (PAYG, 6mo commit, 12mo commit) plus the vendor docs, we can start finance approval immediately. Our initial expectation is to approve a pilot (pay-as-you-go) quickly; approvals for committed spend will follow once we have forecasts.

Thanks,
Dana Li
Senior Procurement Manager, FinHub
dana.li@finhub.com

Attachment: procurement-reqs.pdf
